title: Local coherent acyclicity on sufficiently small polydiscs

items.title: Refinement-limit Čech cohomology computes derived sheaf cohomology on metric spaces
items.physical_scope: A general theorem on ordinary sheaf cohomology; no physical model or empirical claim is involved.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Sheaf cohomology and the De Rham-Weil isomorphism theorem
references.locator: §1.A–1.C, printed/PDF pp. 1–5: refinement-limit Čech cohomology, the paracompact cochain-lifting lemma, and Leray comparison; complete relevant arguments read.

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space and let
$\mathcal F$ be a sheaf of abelian groups on its metric topology. Define
$\check H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ as the filtered colimit of the fixed-cover ordered
Čech cohomology groups over all open covers, and define $H^q(X,\mathcal F)$ as
the right derived functors of global sections from an injective resolution.
Then the canonical comparison
$$\check H^q(X,\mathcal F)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal F)$$
is a natural isomorphism for every integer $q\ge0$, compatible with the
identity identification of both degree-zero groups with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$.

items.title: Locally finite refinements of Euclidean open covers have order at most the dimension plus one
items.physical_scope: A topological theorem about Euclidean open sets; no physical model or empirical claim is involved.

references.title: Ian Agol, Complex Analysis and Riemann Surfaces, course notes
references.locator: §6, Theorem 6.5, printed/PDF p. 29: the sheaf-dimension vanishing theorem is stated from fine covers with empty (m+2)-fold intersections; the refinement construction is supplied in this item.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Chapter IX §4.B, printed/PDF p. 421: the local acyclicity proof uses topological dimension at most real dimension; this item proves the needed Euclidean refinement bound directly.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$ and let $\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset of
$\mathbb R^m$ with its Euclidean metric. For every open cover $\mathcal U$ of
$\Omega$, there is a locally finite open cover $\mathcal V$ and a refinement
map $\rho:\mathcal V\to\mathcal U$ with $V\subseteq\rho(V)$ for every
$V\in\mathcal V$, such that each point of $\Omega$ lies in at most $m+1$
members of $\mathcal V$. Here locally finite means that every point has an
open neighborhood meeting only finitely many members, and the order bound
means the stated pointwise multiplicity bound.

items.title: Ordinary sheaf cohomology on Euclidean open sets vanishes above real dimension
items.physical_scope: A bound for ordinary derived sheaf cohomology on Euclidean open sets; no physical model or empirical claim is involved.

references.title: Ian Agol, Complex Analysis and Riemann Surfaces, course notes
references.locator: §6, Vanishing theorem by dimension, Theorem 6.5, printed/PDF p. 29; the local proof supplies the refinement and derived Čech comparison arguments.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Chapter IX §4.B, Lemma 4.4 proof, printed/PDF p. 421: the dimension-shift argument requires ordinary cohomological dimension at most real dimension.

items.statement:
Assume full AC. Let $m\ge1$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be a nonempty
open subset with its Euclidean metric, and let $\mathcal G$ be any sheaf of
abelian groups on $\Omega$. Then ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology
satisfies
$$H^q(\Omega,\mathcal G)=0\qquad\text{for every integer }q>m.$$
This is an ordinary cohomology bound for arbitrary sheaves; it is not a
compact-support cohomology assertion.

items.title: Local coherent acyclicity on sufficiently small polydiscs
items.physical_scope: Pure local complex analytic sheaf cohomology under the Axiom of Choice; no physical model or empirical claim is made.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Chapter IX §4.A, Proposition 4.1, and §4.B, equation (4.3) and Lemma 4.4 with its complete proof, printed pp. 419–421: partial local free resolutions, scalar polydisc vanishing, and dimension shift. The proof here supplies the ordinary sheaf cohomological-dimension bound explicitly.

references.title: Joachim Wehler, Stein Manifolds
references.locator: §5.2, Proposition 5.9, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15, printed pp. 171–180: acyclicity from a finite free resolution, coherent free resolutions after shrinking to a relatively compact polydisc, and the resulting coherent-sheaf vanishing. This corroborates the conclusion; no full finite resolution is used by the partial-resolution proof here.

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let $N\ge0$, let $U$ be an open neighborhood
of $x\in\mathbb C^N$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent analytic
$\mathcal O_U$-module. A coordinate polydisc centered at $x$ means a set
$$W=\{z\in\mathbb C^N:|z_j-x_j|<r_j\ (1\le j\le N)\},\qquad r_j>0,$$
contained in $U$. There is such a $W$ for which the following hold.

For every nonempty coordinate polydisc $D\subseteq W$ and every integer
$q>0$, ordinary derived-functor sheaf cohomology satisfies
$$H^q(D,\mathcal F|_D)=0.$$
On each such $D$, scalar sheaf cohomology of $\mathcal O_D$ is computed by the
global smooth Dolbeault complex. Here $\mathcal A_D^{0,q}$ is the sheaf of
smooth complex-valued differential forms of type $(0,q)$ and $\bar\partial$ is
the Dolbeault differential:
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,0})\xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\cdots \xrightarrow{\bar\partial}\Gamma(D,\mathcal A_D^{0,N}),$$
and in particular $H^q(D,\mathcal O_D)=0$ for $q>0$. The polydisc $W$ may be
chosen inside a neighborhood on which there is a partial finite-rank free resolution
$$\mathcal O_W^{p_\ell}\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow \mathcal O_W^{p_0}\longrightarrow\mathcal F|_W\longrightarrow0$$
that is exact at $\mathcal F|_W$ and at every free term except possibly the
leftmost one, with $\ell=2N+1>2N$. No exactness at the leftmost term and no
global free resolution are asserted.

title: Local coherent acyclicity on sufficiently small polydiscs — Examples

items.title: A point-supported coherent quotient on a polydisc
items.physical_scope: A local complex analytic sheaf example; no physical model or empirical claim is made.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Chapter IX §4.B, pp. 419–421: local coherent-sheaf vanishing; the quotient identification is verified here by stalks.

references.title: Joachim Wehler, Stein Manifolds
references.locator: §5.2, Theorem 5.14 and Corollary 5.15, printed pp. 174–180: coherent-sheaf vanishing on sufficiently small polydiscs.

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice, let $N\ge1$, and on a neighborhood $U$ of
$0\in\mathbb C^N$ define the coherent quotient
$\mathcal Q_U=\mathcal O_U/(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\mathcal O_U$. Let $W$ be a
coordinate polydisc supplied by the local coherent-acyclicity theorem for
$\mathcal Q_U$. For any nonempty coordinate polydisc $D\subseteq W$ containing
$0$, set
$$\mathcal Q=\mathcal O_D/(z_1,\ldots,z_N)\mathcal O_D.$$
Then $\mathcal Q$ is coherent and the evaluation morphism identifies it with
the skyscraper sheaf $i_*\mathbb C$ at $i:\{0\}\hookrightarrow D$. Consequently
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal Q)\cong\mathbb C,\qquad H^q(D,\mathcal Q)=0\quad(q>0).$$

items.title: A hyperplane-supported coherent quotient on a polydisc
items.physical_scope: A local complex analytic sheaf example; no physical model or empirical claim is made.

references.title: Jean-Pierre Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry
references.locator: Chapter IX §4.A, Proposition 4.1, printed pp. 419–420: scalar acyclicity on strongly 1-complete domains. The quotient identification and global multiplication-sequence proof are verified here.

references.title: Joachim Wehler, Stein Manifolds
references.locator: §5.2, Proposition 5.9, printed p. 171: a sheaf with a finite free resolution on a polydisc is acyclic; the multiplication sequence supplies such a resolution in this example.

items.statement:
Assume the full Axiom of Choice and let $N\ge1$. Let $D\subseteq\mathbb C^N$
be any coordinate polydisc containing $0$: thus $D=\prod_{j=1}^N B(a_j,r_j)$
with $r_j>0$ and $|a_j|<r_j$ for every $j$. Its coordinate discs need not be
centered at $0$. Define
$$H_D=D\cap\{z_1=0\},\qquad i:H_D\hookrightarrow D,$$
and set $\mathcal Q=\mathcal O_D/(z_1)\mathcal O_D$. Then $\mathcal Q$ is
coherent and restriction to the hyperplane induces an isomorphism
$$\mathcal Q\cong i_*\mathcal O_{H_D}.$$
The multiplication sequence
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_D\xrightarrow{\ \cdot z_1\ }\mathcal O_D\longrightarrow\mathcal Q\longrightarrow0$$
is exact, and
$$\Gamma(D,\mathcal Q)\cong\mathcal O(H_D),\qquad H^q(D,\mathcal Q)=0\quad(q>0).$$
In particular the global sections are the actual quotient
$\mathcal O(D)/z_1\mathcal O(D)$, identified with holomorphic functions on
$H_D$. All cohomology here is ordinary derived global-sections cohomology;
no small-neighborhood restriction or general coherent Stein vanishing is assumed.
